ruling.explanation:
To both of you: the trip ran 13.52 km against a platform optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.12 km, or 30% — and that passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km). But the excess is entirely explained by the stop the rider asked for, so there is no deviation left to refund and the charge of SGD 19.69 stands. The ruling is NO_ACTION and the SGD 4.00 of disputed fare is not returned.

Rider: your own chat message at 10:19:39 — 'can we stop at Paya Lebar Square first, need to grab something' — is a rider instruction naming a specific place, sent before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, and the driver accepted it at 10:19:59. The GPS trace shows the vehicle passing within 36 m of the waypoint the platform resolved from your message (Paya Lebar Square), well inside POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration threshold. POL-RD-04 excludes the distance of a rider-requested detour before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied, and with the detour removed the remaining excess is nil, so no refund is due. Your characterisation that you 'only asked for a quick stop, not a tour' does not change the clause's test: the place you named is the reason for the extra distance and the driver drove to it. For transparency, had the detour not been rider-requested the POL-RD-02 recomputation would have been charged_total 19.69 less recomputed_fare 16.32, a refund of SGD 3.40; that computation does not run here because POL-RD-04 removes the excess. POL-RD-11 does not apply — the fare is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE.

Driver: your arithmetic and the rider-advocate's are right. An excess of 3.12 km / 30% is above the 20% / 0.8 km gate but below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality line, so the POL-RD-06 uplift and conduct referral are not triggered. Your profile is clean on the only counters POL-RD-06 permits — deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 368 — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has not been used. No driver compensation is due: the ledger bills 13.5 km against a trace of 13.52 km, a shortfall of 0.02 km, below the 1.0 km threshold in POL-RD-04. No ERP gantries and no airport surcharge were charged, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct.

On the evidence: the GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 107 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so the deviation measurement and its removal both rest on a clean trace. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02812-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); neither side asserted an external traffic cause, so under POL-RD-13 its absence is a gap in the bundle and not a contradiction, and it does not trigger POL-RD-10(5). Two claims that cited that artifact without disclosing its impairment were discarded by the referee.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding fact — that the Paya Lebar Square stop was requested by the rider — is carried by the chat log (EV-CHAT-02812, weight 1.0) and independently by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02812, weight 1.0), so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the platform-wide floor of 0.70 is met. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. The monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
